title: AjsLearningTools Plugin
eyebrow: Plan for approval · nothing built yet

short.lead: A new repo, AjsLearningTools, holds one Claude Code plugin with a lesson skill. You give it a link or the next topic in a course. It writes a plain lesson, has a separate agent check it against the source, fixes what fails, and builds the lesson page. The two sections you called mature are saved as fixed templates, and the other sections stay marked as drafts.

The lesson skill (SKILL.md)
Runs the pipeline in fixed steps.

The skill has five steps, plus a loop that fixes and rechecks any claim that fails. First, it gets the source page. Second, it writes the lesson from the baseline rules. Third, a separate agent checks each claim in the lesson against the source. If a claim fails, it is rewritten and checked again. Fourth, it builds the page and checks sentence length, filler words and picture safety. Fifth, it saves the lesson and shows you the page. It never asks you to read the source yourself.
The steps exist as a prompt file I follow by hand.
A skill Claude follows the same way every time.
Each lesson takes one command instead of a long conversation.

Templates: stable and draft
Your two mature sections are frozen.

templates/stable/ holds the two parts you called mature: the gist, written to the baseline rules (plain language for anyone, with no background assumed), and the New words first format, including the Other meanings part. Lesson 1's System and Component entries serve as the reference example. templates/draft/ holds the other six parts: Why you care, Think of it like this, The core idea, Picture it, Where it is used, and Check yourself. The skill follows stable templates exactly and treats drafts as its current best guess.
One prompt file where finished and unfinished rules sit side by side.
Stable rules in one folder and draft rules in another.

choices: Should the repo be public or private?
Matches your other plugin repos, installs without signing in, and is ready for open source later.
Only you can see it; installing needs GitHub sign-in on each machine.
Your other plugin repos are public, and the open-source app comes next anyway.
What should you type to start a lesson?
For example: /learn next, or /learn followed by a link.
Short, and it names the action you are taking (learning) rather than the thing you get (a lesson).
Where should lessons and course progress be saved?
A lessons folder in the project you run it from
Each course can live in its own folder or repo, and it syncs the same way that folder does.
One fixed folder in your home folder
Every course is in one place on each machine, but nothing syncs between machines.
Keeps your lessons wherever you already work, and works the same on every machine.
Should the first version track a course in order?
/learn next works from day one, starting with the first topic of the System Design tutorial.
A smaller first version; you name each topic yourself.
You said you want to learn every day, and "next" saves you from finding the topic each time.
